  environment, while being sensitive to the diversity of our community.

  CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) ADVISORY NOTICE

not be physically open to the public, although the public may participate by video conference or

rather than in person.

   CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  REGULAR MEETING
  ALHAMBRA ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY COMMISSION

  City Hall, 111 South First Street
  JANUARY 12, 2023
  6:00 p.m.

  I.  ROLL CALL
  John Vuong, Kim Luu, Katie Chan, Karla Grijalva, Lisa Massaro

  II.  ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY MEETING MINUTES 11-10-22
  Commission Members will vote to approve 11-10-22 meeting minutes.
  Recommended Action: Approve the meeting minutes.

  III.  UPDATE ITEMS
  a) Sustainability Plan
  b) Turf Replacement Rebate
  c) Pedestrian and Bike Plan
  d) Leaf Blower Ban
  Recommended Action: Information only. No action required

  IV.  EFFICIENT SAN GABRIEL VALLEY PROGRAM PRESENTATION
  The San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments will provide information on the Efficient San
  Gabriel Valley (eSGV) program which provides free in-home or online energy efficiency reviews
  for renters and homeowners in the SGV. eSGV reviews help residents identify long and short-
  term opportunities for energy savings in their homes. Residents who participate in the program
  will receive a customized, in-depth report energy efficiency recommendations, as well as
  extensive information on applicable rebate and incentive programs.
  Recommended Action: Information only. No action required.

  V.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments are welcome, but
  must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please
  limit all oral communication to five (5) minutes. Speakers must fill out a blue speaker’s card, prior
  to the meeting and submit it to the Commission Secretary. Comments must pertain to the business
  of the Environmental Sustainability Commission. Please limit all oral communications to five (5)
  minutes.

  VI.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION
  Discussion from the Commission Members of any item not specified on the agenda and agenda
  items for next meeting. Items must pertain to the business of the Alhambra Environmental
  Sustainability Commission.
  Recommended Action: Discussion only. No action required.

  VII.  ADJOURNMENT
  Adjournment to the next regular meeting on Thursday, November 10, 2022 at 6:00 p.m.

  MINUTES
  Environmental Sustainability Commission
  Regular Meeting of November 10, 2022

  The regular meeting of the Environmental Sustainability Commission was called to
  order at 6:12 p.m. on November 10, 2022 through Zoom teleconferencing.

  I.  Roll Call
  Commission Members Present: Chan, Grijalva, Massaro

  Commission Members Absent: Luu, Vuong

  Staff Present:  Latoya Waters (on behalf of David Dolphin) – Commission Secretary

  Members of the Public

  Craig Cadwallader – Policy Coordinator Surfrider Foundation South Bay
  Sandy Lee – Alhambra Resident (info@smarttimerrebate.com)

 II.  VOTE TO APPROVE MEETING MINUTES FROM 9/8/22
  Commissioner Chan motioned to approve the meeting minutes from 9/8/22.
  Commissioner Grijalva seconded the motion. All Commissioners present voted in
  favor to approve the minutes. Motion to approve passed.

III.  UPDATE ITEMS
  Provided in the Agenda packets, verbally provided by the City as follows:
  A. Sustainability Plan
  • The City has received the funding agreement documents from HUD
  and will go to Council to approve a solicitation to release a Request for
  Proposal to develop the Sustainability Plan.

  B. Tree Ordinance
  • The City does replace diseased or hazardous trees in the public right-of
  way. The property owner must agree to maintain the tree.
  • The City replaces approximately 75 trees every year.
  • The reason why there is no requirement to replace a diseased or
  hazardous tree on private property is to avoid placing an undue
  hardship on a property owner to replace the tree.
  • It is the City’s understanding that it is not the fault of the owner and
  often times a tree has reached its maximum life span.

  Page 1 of 6
   ITEM #2
  • In response to John’s (Commissioner Vuong) Comments at the last
  meeting:
  City Tree Planting Events:
  1. April 2021 (50 trees planted)
  2. September 2022 (25 trees planted)
  Donated by a nursery in Irvine and planted by volunteers from
  Stanbridge University.

  C. Turf Replacement Rebate
  • The San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District (SGVMWD) is
  interested in applying for the DWR Drought Relief Grant to provide
  assistance to its member agencies to fund a turf replacement rebate
  program. The City of Alhambra has expressed interest and provided
  feedback to the SGVMWD.

  D. Recycling Event
  Below are some statistics from the Alhambra Recycles Event October
  2022:
  • Total Car Tally: 369
  • Plastic Bottles & Aluminum Cans: 16 (4.3% of cars)
  • Document Shredding: 130 (35.2% of cars)
  • Electronic Waste: 240 (65% of cars)
  • Compost Giveaway: 115 (31.2% of cars)
  • Paint Collection: 245 cars
  • Collected approximately 17500 lbs. of latex
  • Collected approximately 2580 lbs. of OBP
  • Gave away 58 gallons of reused paint

  The City is definitely interested in having more compost giveaways. We
  currently have two Alhambra Recycles Events a year in which we
  distribute compost (October and April), but they do take a lot of planning
  and budgeting and the City doesn’t foresee having more events per year at
  this scale. However, we have been looking for other ways to distribute
  more compost. Some ideas have been to distribute it at the Community
  Garden or Weekly Farmers Market. We would welcome volunteers if you
  are interested.

IV. ZERO WASTE EVENTS

  The City of LA is creating zero waste events and zero-waste facilities and every
  employee will be trained on zero waste. They are also banning polystyrene and sales
  of single-use plastic water bottles. Alhambra should encourage refill stores to come to
  our city and organizations to provide these zero waste events.

  Commissioner Chan stated, the City of LA is doing tremendous work in their Farmer’s
  Market, in comparison to Alhambra’s Farmer’s Market. Alhambra can also do so

  Page 2 of 6
   ITEM #2
  much more during the Farmer’s Market events, such as composting, seasoning
  groceries, bee keeping. The City should provide opportunities to learn more about the
  Environment and engage residents in multiple languages. Also, provide resources such
  as grants and assistance to apply for these grants.

  New compost refill locations are opening in LA. The closest compost refill store is in
  Monrovia Farmer’s Market, having a permanent store in Alhambra would be amazing.
  Commissioner Chan indicated that she is in discussion with “Sustain LA” and
  “re_grocery” to come on this side (closer to Alhambra), as most of them are open on
  the Westside of LA County in cities such as Culver City. Asking if the City could
  assist in navigating these types of stores to the City.

  Commissioner Chan asked for thoughts from attendees. Sandy Lee has raised her hand
  for comment. She is excited about a zero-waste store and would love to volunteer to
  assist any efforts. She is will to assist with campaigns, classes, etc. Asking to meet, if
  necessary, she is excited to help Alhambra.

  Sandy is a home composter, recruits interns for a composting site at the Rose Bowl,
  and everything is reused in a closed loop system. She is happy to talk to anyone about
  this.

  Commissioner Grijalva stated she echoes Sandy’s comments and is a huge fan of
  educational outreach in the City for composting and zero waste. We should create a
  good base for the community to move forward, starting with education.

  Staff informed the Commissioners and public attendees that the County offers Free
  Smart Gardening Classes throughout the entire County in various cities. Compost bins
  with and without worms are sold at subsidized pricing for attendees. The next
  workshop will be in South Pasadena Saturday November 19. Additional information is
  available on the following websites: www.cleanla.com or www.smartgardening.com.

  Commissioner Massaro stated she would be very interested in attending a workshop or
  class. We should collaborate with Sandy Lee and perhaps she can teach a class?

  Commissioner Grijalva stated that the information should be available in the
  newspaper sources throughout the City. Provide information to the community about
  the classes.

  Commissioner Chan stated that the commission as a whole should suggest to council
  a ban of polystyrene and single use plastic water bottles within the City of Alhambra.
  Establish and encourage refill stores in the City of Alhambra. Assist in locating an
  accessible location(s) for the store(s).

V.  BAN LEAF BLOWERS

  New CA state law bans the sale of gas-powered leaf blowers by the start of 2024. As
  part of that law, $30 million will be made available to sole proprietors and other small

  Page 3 of 6
   ITEM #2
  landscaping businesses to assist in the purchase of zero-emission small off-road
  equipment, including leaf-blowing machines, lawnmowers, and string trimmers.
  Commission will discuss options for the City of Alhambra.

  Commissioner Chan wants to bring this to Council and put together a timeline to ban
  leaf blowers efficiently and equitably by 2024. Also educate those affected by this ban.
  She furthered that questions are arising:
  • How will the proposed $30M be distributed to the City of Alhambra?
  • How do we inform the community about these available funds?
  • Is the full amount of equipment covered?
  • Does the Council have a plan and timeline for implementation?

  Commissioner Grijalva agrees with Commissioner Chan in creating opportunities to
  assist our community. Assistance and guidance should be provided for equipment
  swapping and recommended to keep the program assistance within the Alhambra
  community.

VI.  FRONT YARD OPTION TO REMOVE TURF
  Commission will discuss options available to replace front yard turf for residents in
  accordance with AMC Chapter 23.48.

  Commissioner Chan stated that in review of the referenced Chapter, landscaping
  standards. She does not like artificial turf (turf).

  Commissioner Grijalva stated that artificial turf smells when it is hot and still needs to
  be watered down. If the community is able to have drought tolerant plants as opposed
  to turf, that would be preferred. Resources that are necessary to produce an artificial
  system could be a source of contamination in the future. Additional research is
  necessary. There may be locations where turf is suitable, such as schools and large
  fields, but not in residential/multi-family.

  Commissioner Chan stated that the ordinance proposes unsustainability. Maintenance
  for artificial turf does not sound good in reading the ordinance.

  Commissioner Massaro also agrees that the turf is not good for residential. The smell
  of animal wastes and discharges on the turf should also be considered. The turf may be
  uneven and “lumpy” after a while. Drought resistant is a better option, especially in
  consideration of beautification efforts.

  Commissioner Chan understands the shift from usage of sand and dirt in front lawns.
  Normalizing usage of rocks and pebbles for lawn beautification. She can provide some
  examples from areas in City of LA. East Los Angeles Community College (ELACC)
  had their entire campus renovating with drought tolerant landscaping and trees. Maybe
  not a front yard covered with rocks, but a good balance. Not proposing complete
  elimination of turf but not having an entire lawn of turf. Dead grass is not aesthetically
  pleasing but turf is also not aesthetically pleasing.

  Page 4 of 6
   ITEM #2
  Commissioner Grijalva asked if the reference to “sand” is decomposed granite or
  something similar?

  Commissioner Chan responded, yes, the dirt on the ground that is yellowish in color.

  Commissioner Grijalva discussed the variabilities with decomposed granite, permeable
  pavers, and planting on lawns. Also, incentives should be more available.

  Commissioner Chan agreed and indicated that this may be more accessible and cost
  effective, regenerating the soil is healthy and promotes water absorption in the soil.

  Commissioner Grijalva: another key point, these gardens can provide a means for
  pollination and restore natural habit systems that have been denied to thrive. Some
  microsystems are still around, but drought tolerant could offer a richer system.

  Commissioner Chan: native plants, bees and butterflies (our natural pollinators) are
  going extinct. There’s a big misconception of using pesticides to make the process of
  growing faster, that is not necessarily the case. There are many insects and bugs that
  perform as pesticides do to promote growth. Gradually reintroducing and regenerating
  a natural cycle of how the ecosystem works to use less pesticides and possibly
  completely eliminate usage. There are some situations where pesticides can be used to
  control diseased plants… however, we will stop here and continue this discussion at
  our next meeting and bring before Council to see what are their thoughts to assure
  everyone is on the same page.

VII.  PUBLIC COMMENT

  Craig Cadwallader
  Policy Coordinator
  Surfrider Foundation - Southbay Chapter
  craigc@surfrider-southbay.org
  424-6340452

  Craig: Wants to thank everyone for bringing forth the recommended comprehensive
  Plastic Waste Reduction Ordinance at the last meeting. Comments were made in the
  meeting minutes that suggest the next step is to present to City Council, but there were
  no discussions on timelines or next steps. Nearly identical ordinances are being looked
  at in the Cities of Glendale, Burbank, and Pasadena. These cities expressed that they
  would like to see similar ordinances in all neighboring cities. For reference the City of
  Glendale will bring its ordinance on November 29 for its first reading, Burbak is
  possibly scheduled for January 31, for the first reading. He would love to see a
  timeline or next steps decided on by the Commission. Craig is available to provide
  assistance. An ordinance has recently been adopted in Goleta, which was mentioned
  in the September meeting minutes. The City of Los Angeles City Council approved
  amendments to a polystyrene to possibly be passed by the end of 2022.
  Unincorporated LA County has passed their comprehensive ordinance on April 19,
  2022.

  Page 5 of 6
   ITEM #2

  Surfrider would love to have Alhambra and surrounding cities operate from similar
  ordinances.

  Requesting a timeline to see this to Council and is glad to provide any assistance
  including ordinance development.

VIII.  COMMISSION COMMUNICATION

  Commissioner Chan: Is also requesting a timeline, when can the Commission present
  to Council? Climate change is urgent and implementing a Plastic Waste Reduction
  Ordinance is the first step forward. Requesting the availability of Council Members.

  Update when Commission can meet with Council.

  Commissioner Chan: Christmas tree pick ups have been more effective in the City.
  Is the City still doing this service? Where can more information be obtained.
  Normalize DIY projects and reuse opportunities with kids and the community.

  Commissioner Massaro: will check up on the details of pumpkin and Christmas tree
  recycling in the City.

  Commissioner Grijalva: agrees with Commissioner Chan to implement waste
  reduction strategies during the holidays. Other cultures may exercise such strategies.
  Begin with education, discussions at school how to reduce waste.

  Also, question about the Sustainability Plan Update? Is the RFP out? What is the
  process? Will the Commission participate in the selection process?

  Commissioner Chan: From the last agenda it states that the City is waiting for HUD
  to develop the plan.

  Staff mentioned: The City has received the funding agreement documents from HUD
  and prior to releasing RFPs we have to get approval from Council. The next step is to
  go to Council to approve a solicitation to release a Request for Proposal to develop
  the Sustainability Plan.

  Commissioner Grijalva: Can the Commissioners participate in the RFP development
  and selection process?

  Commissioner Chan: The Commissioners will be very hopeful to participate in the
  process.

 IX.  ADJOURNMENT

  Commissioner Chan motioned to adjourn the meeting at 6:54 PM, Commissioner
  Grijalva seconded. Motion unanimously approved. Meeting adjourned at 6:55 PM.

Environmental Sustainability Commission Meeting- January 12, 2023
Update Items

  1. Sustainability Plan

  Staff received Council authorization to solicit proposals from qualified firms for the development
  of the Plan. Proposals were originally expected back mid-January; however, due to the holiday
  period, the deadline has been extended to February 9, 2023. Thereafter, we will proceed with
  the selection process including interviews. The Council presentation for award of contract is
  tentative for March 13, 2023. We are hoping for a start period of April 2023.

  A Council Ad Hoc Committee will likely help with screening and selection. Once a consultant is
  awarded and the plan approach has been finalized and negotiated, the Environmental
  Commission will be given more information, including feedback on how the
  communication/engagement components will be conducted. Certainly, there will be various
  workshops and public meetings for which the Environmental Commission will be invited to
  participate. Near the end of the process, the draft plan will be submitted to the Environmental
  Commission as well as other Commissions.

  2. Turf Replacement Rebate

  The San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District (SGVMWD) is planning to apply for the DWR
  Drought Relief Grant to provide assistance to its member agencies to fund a turf replacement
  rebate program. The application deadline is January 31, 2023 and a consultant has been hired
  to complete the application process. The City of Alhambra has expressed interest in the
  program.

  3. Pedestrian and Bike Plan

  The City of Alhambra is developing the Walk, Bike, Move Alhambra! Plan to improve the quality
  of life for residents, workers, and visitors by providing improved facilities to allow people to
  walk and bike throughout the city. Your input is vital in developing the project
  recommendations, policies, and priorities of this Plan. Share your ideas for walking, biking, and
  rolling in Alhambra via the public input map and take the survey by January 31, 2023.
  https://walkbikemovealhambra.altaplanning.cloud/

  The City is also seeking participants in a Walking Audit and Bicycling Audit:
  Walking Audit will take place Saturday, January 21 at 10 a.m. Meeting location is Alhambra Civic
  Center Library, 101 S 1st St, Alhambra, CA 91801.

  Registration required through the link: forms.gle/fV1qwEp5ZuKo5mEn6

  Biking Audit will take place Saturday, January 28 at 10 a.m. Meeting location is Alhambra Civic
  Center Library, 101 S 1st St, Alhambra, CA 91801

  Registration required through the link: forms.gle/fV1qwEp5ZuKo5mEn6
  Please contact Danielle Zamora at danielle@activesgv.org or (626) 388-6809 with any questions.
   ITEM #3

4. Leaf Blower Ban

  City staff began using electric leaf blowers (on a limited basis during the last 2‐3 years) for the
  maintenance of public spaces. Limited, because the technology is such that on substantial
  landscape (ie, parks), there is NOT sufficient battery power to enable the completion of work. As
  the technology improves, the goal of the City is to fully utilize electric options.

  The new law only bans sales of new gas‐driven leaf blowers. In 2024, all new machinery must
  meet zero emission standards; however, it does not eliminate leaf blowers already being used
  by private persons. To that end, as part of the City’s sustainability efforts, an education
  campaign is expected to ensue to adequately inform residents of the smog‐forming emissions
  caused by gas‐powered equipment.
